newsitem.title: BRAZIL: No delay expected for Brazil CVRD auction - Borges.
newsitem.headline: No delay expected for Brazil CVRD auction - Borges.

text.p: The vice-president of Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES), Jose Pio Borges, said he did not expect any delay in the privatization auction of state mining giant CVRD, now set for April 29.

A formal accusation alleging conflict of interest involving U.S. investment bank Merrill Lynch and Co Inc, which acted as consultant to the Brazilian government on the CVRD privatization, has been presented to the BNDES and could lead to an inquiry.

Borges said the bank was looking into the matter to see whether it was legally obliged to carry out an inquiry, but he did not think such an inquiry would lead to a delay of the privatization auction.
"If we have to do it (probe), we will do it," he said. "I don't believe there will be a delay (of the auction)."
Borges said documents supplied by Merrill Lynch and the Johannesburg stock exchange should be sufficient to refute the accusations.

A group of lower house deputies alleges that Merrill Lynch's ownership of South African brokerage Smith Borkum Hare (SBH) gives South African mining conglomerate and expected CVRD bidder Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd an advantage in the privatization process.
SBH acts as a sponsoring broker for Anglo American on the Johannesburg stock exchange.
Merrill Lynch has rejected the accusations, saying SBH's relationship with Anglo American is merely administrative and not consultative.

It has also denied allegations that it acquired SBH specifically to pass on information on CVRD to Anglo American, saying it gained control of SBH two months prior to its appointment as consultant for the CVRD privatization.

Borges said he expected more than one consortium to bid at the auction of a 45 percent block of CVRD voting shares, which would lead to a premium on the minimum price of three billion reais ($2.83 billion).
"We are absolutely confident that there will be more than one group in the running," he said. "Two are the most likely; three is more difficult. I believe more in two."

He said one consortium forming around Brazilian metal, cement and pulp group Votorantim was already in an advanced stage, while another including Brazil's largest steelmaker CSN and South Africa's Gencor Ltd was also making progress.
Australia's mining company WMC Ltd has also been cited as looking to form a consortium with Japan's Mitsui Co Ltd and Brazilian iron ore miner MBR.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
